quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane ahead, but there is no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the pedestrian, then pass them.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane, even if there is no crosswalk. Pedestrians have the right-of-way.

questions.question: You see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the person is far away from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is far away from your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person using a white cane or guide dog, you must stop. Always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: You just had an argument and feel angry. What should you do before driving?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about the argument.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the highway to calm down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like anger make it harder to drive safely. Calm down before you drive so you can focus on the road.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means drivers should be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge in.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that two lanes will soon become one. Be ready to change lanes or allow other drivers to merge into your lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: What do flashing arrow panels in work zones do?

options.text: Tell drivers to pull onto the shoulder and stop.
Direct drivers into certain lanes and show that part of the road is closed.
Are only used on Interstate highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Direct drivers into certain lanes and show that part of the road is closed.
questions.explanation: Flashing arrow panels guide you into the correct lanes and tell you that part of the road ahead is closed. Follow all signs in work zones.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both the alcohol and drug effects may become stronger.
Nothing happens.
Both effects may become weaker.
Only the alcohol effect becomes weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the alcohol and drug effects may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, having a drink while taking cold medicine can affect you as if you had several drinks.

questions.question: What is true about vehicles with airbags?

options.text: The driver should not wear a safety belt if the car has airbags.
Airbags work best when used with safety belts.
Children age 12 and under can sit safely in the front seat with airbags.

questions.correctAnswerText: Airbags work best when used with safety belts.
questions.explanation: Airbags and safety belts work together for the best protection in a crash. Airbags are an extra safety feature, not a replacement for belts. Children age 12 and under should sit in the back seat because airbags can injure them.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content and its effects.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating high-fat foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and its effects.

questions.question: You should never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers. It is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: A school bus uses flashing red lights when picking up or dropping off students. You must stop and wait until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised. Never pass a school bus that is loading or unloading students.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can go through the intersection. First, yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up the radio volume.
Park in a safe place and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park in a safe place and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Signs of driver fatigue include struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting out of your lane, or turning up the radio to stay awake. If you notice these signs, find a safe place to park and rest.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down; a curving road is ahead.
Slow down and do not use your brakes.
Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction the arrow shows.
A curve is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction the arrow shows.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the direction you must drive. Always drive in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Follow the car in front of you closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on the road. Don't take other drivers' actions personally. Leave enough time for your trip, drive at the speed limit, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. Signaling tells other drivers what you are doing and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop whenever you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful around children. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When driving on major highways:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Don't stare at one thing for more than a few seconds. Keep your eyes moving to avoid highway hypnosis.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the car straight and slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal.
Keep your speed the same and drive straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the gas pedal slowly. Do not use the brakes until you have control of the car. Once the car is steady, brake gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: A driver's license can be revoked if the driver tries to escape arrest for breaking any Nebraska law. Is this true?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Your driver's license can be taken away if you try to avoid arrest or get a ticket by running from a police officer.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the rearview mirror inside the car.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to remove the alcohol over time.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to remove the alcohol over time.
questions.explanation: The only way to reduce your BAC is to wait while your body breaks down the alcohol. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or reduce the effects of alcohol. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.
When turning left or right.
When changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder any time you change your car's position. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.
